name: Zinc Deficiency
description: Zinc is essential for enzyme function, hormone production, and protein synthesis. Deficiency causes stunted growth, short internodes, and chlorotic bands in cereals. It is common in flooded rice and high-phosphorus soils.
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young leaves with broad yellow bands
Shortened internodes giving rosette or bunched appearance
White bud in maize (white or pale yellow emerging leaves)
Delayed maturity and poor grain fill
Brown spots on leaves and stems
causes: High soil pH (alkaline conditions) reducing zinc availability
Excessive phosphorus application inducing zinc deficiency
Flooded conditions in rice reducing zinc uptake
Highly weathered tropical soils low in zinc
treatments: Apply zinc sulfate (ZnSO4) at 10-25 kg/ha as soil application
Foliar spray of zinc sulfate (0.5% solution) for quick correction
Zn-EDTA chelate as foliar spray for efficient uptake
Seed treatment with zinc sulfate (1-2% solution) before planting
prevention: Incorporate zinc in basal fertilizer program
